basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 3:14 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 75. Quare non est interrogatus serpens cur hoc fecerit?-- Resp. Quia forte id non'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 75. Quare non est interrogatus serpens cur hoc fecerit?-- Resp. Quia forte id non sua natura vel voluntate fecerat, sed diabolus de illo et per illum fuerat operatus. Ideo dicitur ei: Super pectus tuum gradieris et terram comedes (Gen. III, 14), siquidem in pectore calliditas nequitiarum ejus indicatur; qui et terram devorat, dum luxuria et libidine peccantium pascitur et delectatur [ Al., dilatatur]. Nam [et] sicut diabolus per serpentem loquebatur, ita et in serpente maledicitur.
